\subsection{Faces and embedding tests of \texorpdfstring{$\Psi_3$}{Psi3}}\label{r1:two-tests}

We first determine which faces of a torus embedding of $\Psi_3$ can meet all of $b,c,d,e$.

\begin{lemma}\label{r1:exterior-faces}
In a torus embedding of $\Psi_3$, let $\mathcal N$ be a closed regular
neighborhood of $\Psi_3$. If $\mathcal N$ has genus one and a face meets
$b,c,d,e$, that face is a disk with attachment sequence
$a,b,a,d,a,c,a,e$, up to cyclic shift and reversal, and the other
two faces have attachment sequences $bc,de$. If $\mathcal N$ has genus zero, any face
meeting $b,c,d,e$ is an annulus with attachment sequences $bc\mid de$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
There are $6\cdot2^4=96$ rotations: six cyclic orders at $a$,
two at each twin, and one at each remaining vertex. Trace their
facial walks, retaining the appearances of $a,b,c,d,e$.
Since $\Psi_3$ has nine vertices and twelve edges, a rotation
with $f$ facial walks has genus $(5-f)/2$.
The results are summarized in~\supp{R6}. In genus one, a walk containing
$b,c,d,e$ has the stated sequence, with the other walks having attachment sequences $bc,de$.
In genus zero, the sequences are $abad,ac,ae,bc,de$, up to
interchanging $b,c$ and interchanging $d,e$.

If $\mathcal N$ has genus one, Lemma~\ref{lem:torus-complement} makes
every face a disk. If $\mathcal N$ has genus zero, no single boundary
walk meets $b,c,d,e$, and the only pair that does is $bc,de$.
The same lemma therefore makes any face meeting these four
vertices an annulus with those boundaries.
\end{proof}
